newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open up $10 to $15 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open up $10 to $15 a tonne.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 to $15 higher Thursday, but dealings were likely to remain subdued, dealers said.

New York cocoa futures settled higher Wednesday in sluggish trading, with July $9 higher at $1,458 a tonne after trading from $1,456 to $1,467. Spot May gained $12 to $1,437, while the deferred months climbed between $8 and $10.
"Every day the market just seems to creep higher, but it's very, very quiet," one trader said. "I think (July) needs to close above $1,480 to look good."
Filling a chart gap overhead from $1,480 to $1,501 would be the next upside objective, traders said, while support is seen at $1,430 and $1,410.
LIFFE cocoa futures mixed by the midday break on Thursday, with nearby contracts firming. May rose seven stg to 1,025 stg per tonne, while July stood eight stg higher to 1,046 stg per tonne.
